newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin, Maskhadov to meet on Chechnya peace.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin, Maskhadov to meet on Chechnya peace.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin and Chechen leader Aslan Maskhadov will meet on Monday to discuss relations between Moscow and the breakaway southern region.
Yeltsin's press office said the meeting would start around noon (0800 GMT), but gave no further details.
Interfax news agency quoted a senior Chechen negotiator as saying Yeltsin and Maskhadov would sign an agreement on future relations between Moscow and Chechnya.
Akhmed Zakayev, who is accompanying Maskhadov to Moscow, described the deal as a peace treaty.

Tens of thousands of people died in an ill-fated Russian military operation to crush Chechnya's independence drive. Russia then withdrew its forces and Chechnya promised not to raise the painful issue of its future status until 2001.

Chechen negotiators have made it clear that they ultimately want full independence -- a status Moscow flatly rules out -- and there has been no indication that the two sides have finally come to terms.
"The negotiation commissions have exhausted their resources and it is now for the presidents to decide," Itar-Tass news agency quoted chief Russian negotiator Ivan Rybkin as saying.
The meeting takes place two days after gunmen kidnapped a Russian television crew in Chechnya.
It was the latest in a series of kidnappings and these, together with two explosions in southern Russia, have complicated the prospects for talks.
Both sides have thrown responsibility for the events on "parties of war" which want to wreck the peace process.
